learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of ten metadata field entries is good or needs work, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** metadata-entry-judge
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of ten metadata field entries is good or needs work, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Title Field, Author Field, Subject Field, Grade Level Field, License Field, Description Field (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each entry the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the field guidance is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Any filled field is a good field. (2) A short entry is always weak. (3) A license field only needs the license's short name. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging an entry against what its field is for is an Evaluate-level action that a reviewer performs when scoring metadata. Ten entries across six fields, half good and half weak, teach the learner what each field needs. **Content:** The two bins: Good, and Needs work. The ten entries: | # | Field | Entry shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Title | Lesson 3 | Needs work | It names no topic and many resources share it. | | 2 | Title | Watershed Basics: A Grade 6 Reading and Quiz | Good | It names the topic, audience, and kind of resource. | | 3 | Author | Lopez, Maria | Good | It names the person in a consistent form. | | 4 | Author | the teacher | Needs work | It names no one, so no one can be credited. | | 5 | Subject | Watersheds; Water cycle; Earth science | Good | The terms are specific and standard. | | 6 | Subject | Science | Needs work | It is too broad to separate the resource from others. | | 7 | Grade level | Grades 6 to 7 | Good | It states the audience in one consistent scheme. | | 8 | License | CC BY | Needs work | It gives no version and no link. | | 9 | License | CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ | Good | It names the license, version, and text. | | 10 | Description | An amazing resource everyone will love! | Needs work | It says nothing about the content. | **Provenance:** The entries are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The guidance follows the chapter sections for each field. **Rules:** Each entry has exactly one correct bin, five per bin. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one field name and entry and the two bins. 2. The learner places the entry in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After entry 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 entries in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This entry is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can judge a metadata entry." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed entry. **Starting State:** The first entry with its field name and the two bins. The question shown is "Does this entry do its field's job?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked examples of titles, subjects, licenses, and descriptions give the same verdicts: Lesson 3 is poor, Science is too broad, CC BY alone is weak, and the amazing-resource description is poor.
